events.did: punted the grenade into the side of the transport van and shoved Mitch back before it blew
events.quote_anchor: Luckily, she had fast reflexes, and just enough time to punt the grenade into the side of the transport van and shove Mitch back before it blew.

events.did: rolled over on the pavement, swapped the damaged body for a new one, and got her hearing back
events.quote_anchor: She rolled over, swapping out the damaged body for a new one, and the sound came rushing back.

events.did: said he saw nothing in the woods and told them they needed to go now
events.quote_anchor: His jaw ticked. His eyes narrowed. “Nothing,” he said at last, turning back toward the pickup. “We need to go. Now.”

events.did: climbed into the front seat of the transport van and tore pieces out of it, ejecting debris onto the road
events.quote_anchor: Mitch, meanwhile, had climbed into the front seat of the transport van, and was now tearing pieces out, ejecting debris onto the road.

events.did: emerged from the van holding up a laptop instead of the missile launcher June had hoped for
events.quote_anchor: “Like this,” he said, triumphantly. June had been hoping for a missile launcher.

events.did: took the passenger seat of the pickup and left Mitch to squeeze into the back with the sedated dog
events.quote_anchor: She hoisted herself up into the passenger seat, leaving Mitch to squeeze his massive form into the back with the dog.

events.did: held Eli at gunpoint on the forest floor and reported into his comm that he had him
events.quote_anchor: “I’ve got him,” Noah said into his comm. Then, “Yes.”

events.did: reached Eli through the earpiece plug and told him they would talk when he returned to EON
events.quote_anchor: “We’ll talk more when you return to EON,” said the voice. “In the meantime, do whatever Noah says.”

relations.did: protected Mitch because he mattered not to her but to Sydney
relations.quote_anchor: she’d protected Mitch because he mattered—not to her, but to Sydney.

relations.did: was Marcella's old right hand, who shielded Mitch from the blast
relations.quote_anchor: The woman—Marcella’s old right hand, June, he realized when he saw her change—absorbed the worst of the damage, shielding Mitch in the process.

relations.did: felt his hold slipping because his body reacted to Gabriel's displeasure even without an order
relations.quote_anchor: A strange feeling, like a chill, rolled over him. The words were not an order, yet, but his body reacted to the displeasure in the EO’s voice.

relations.did: followed Noah away not because he had no choice but because he knew exactly where Victor was headed
relations.quote_anchor: And Eli followed, not because he had no choice, but because he knew exactly where Victor was headed.

numbers.did: said the grenade cost her one of the bodies in her closet, one she was quite fond of
numbers.quote_anchor: Besides, it had only cost her one of the bodies in her closet.

numbers.did: stopped ten feet away from Noah and Eli and stared into the trees
numbers.quote_anchor: Victor stopped ten feet away and stared into the trees.

numbers.did: made Eli turn and walk away only after the three of them had climbed into the pickup truck
numbers.quote_anchor: Only once the three of them had climbed into the pickup truck did Noah force Eli to turn and walk away.

numbers.did: had a deep scratch on one cheek with a line of blood running from temple to jaw
numbers.quote_anchor: Up close, she noted he had a deep scratch on one cheek, a line of blood running from temple to jaw.

numbers.did: swapped the damaged body for a new one after the explosion blew out her eardrums
numbers.quote_anchor: She rolled over, swapping out the damaged body for a new one, and the sound came rushing back.
